hints: Focus on what hot, concentrated KMnO4 does to a C=C bond, it cleaves it completely and oxidises each carbon separately.
Recall the pattern: a C with two alkyl groups becomes a ketone, while a C with one H becomes a carboxylic acid.
Check each alkene for the pattern R2C=CH-R, with one doubly bonded carbon having no H and the other having one H.
walkthrough:
**Recall oxidative cleavage rule**

Hot, concentrated, acidified KMnO4 breaks the C=C bond completely. Each C of the double bond is oxidised on its own.

$$\text{>C=CH- } \rightarrow \text{ ketone + carboxylic acid}$$

**Translate the rule to substitution**

Count alkyl groups on each C=C carbon. $\text{R}_2\text{C}=$ gives a ketone $\text{R}_2\text{C=O}$. $\text{R-CH}=$ gives a carboxylic acid $\text{R-COOH}$. $\text{=CH}_2$ would give $\text{CO}_2$.

So we need a trisubstituted alkene of type $\text{R}_2\text{C=CH-R}$ to get one ketone plus one acid.

**Analyse compounds 1, 2 and 3**

Compound 1 is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CH-CH(CH}_3)_2$. Left C has two $\text{CH}_3$ groups, right C has one H. Cleavage gives $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=O}$ plus $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-COOH}$.

Compound 2 is $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-CH=C(CH}_2)_4$. Left C has one H, right C has two ring bonds. Cleavage gives $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-COOH}$ plus cyclopentanone.

Compound 3 is $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH=C(CH}_3)\text{-CH(CH}_3)_2$. Left C has one H, right C has two alkyl groups. Cleavage gives $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ plus a ketone.

All three give one carboxylic acid and one ketone.

options.A: Correct. All of 1, 2 and 3 are trisubstituted alkenes of the form R2C=CH-R. Each gives a ketone from the R2C end and a carboxylic acid from the CH-R end on hot concentrated oxidative cleavage.
options.B: Incorrect. This omits compound 3. Compound 3 is CH3-CH=C(CH3)-CH(CH3)2, which is also R-CH=C-R2, so it also gives ethanoic acid plus a ketone. It should be included.
options.C: Incorrect. This omits compound 1. Compound 1 is (CH3)2C=CH-CH(CH3)2, which is also R2C=CH-R, so it gives propanone type ketone plus a carboxylic acid. It should be included.
options.D: Incorrect. This includes only compound 1. Both compounds 2 and 3 also have one C with two alkyl groups and one C with one hydrogen, so both also produce a ketone plus a carboxylic acid.
